sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: राज्ञाम् राजा राजराजः; राजराजेन अर्चिता राजराजार्चिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: rājñām rājā rājarājaḥ; rājarājena arcitā rājarājārcitā
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: rājñām rājā 'the king of kings' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). The first rājan loses its n in composition (Pāṇini 8.2.7 nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya); the second, as the final of a tatpuruṣa, takes the samāsānta suffix ṭac (5.4.91 rājāhaḥsakhibhyaṣ ṭac), so the stem is rājarāja. Outer layer: the participle arcitā 'worshipped' is the head, and the king of kings stands to it in the instrumental as the agent.

components.note: first member; its n drops in composition (rāja-)
head of the inner compound; with the samāsānta ṭac it becomes rāja, giving rājarāja 'king of kings'

names.meaning: She who is worshipped by the King of kings
names.significance: Rājarāja 'king of kings' is a standard name of Kubera, lord of wealth (so the Amarakośa), and Kubera is counted traditionally among the great worshippers of Śrīvidyā. The name also implies that every sovereign's power is received from Her.
names.previous_split_issues: The split cut rāja | rājārcitā; the compound is rāja-rāja 'king of kings' + arcitā 'worshipped', with the a + a fused.

components.note: feminine of rājan 'king' (rājan + ṅīp; the a of -an is dropped: rājñī)

names.meaning: She who is the Queen
names.significance: Traditionally read with the previous name: She is the consort of the King of kings, Śiva as Kāmeśvara, and the ruling queen in Her own right.

meaning_check.note: The name says only 'queen'; 'of Śiva, the Lord of all kings' is the traditional sense and is given under significance.

components.meaning: lovely, delightful; to be delighted in
components.note: √ram 'to delight, rejoice' with the gerundive suffix -ya, feminine

names.meaning: She who is lovely and delightful
names.significance: Traditionally, all that delights the mind delights because of Her; She is the one whose beauty draws the devotee.

meaning_check.note: ramyā is a gerundive, 'to be delighted in, lovely'; 'gives delight' is causative and not in the form.

samasa.vigraha: राजीवे इव लोचने यस्याः सा राजीवलोचना
samasa.vigraha_iast: rājīve iva locane yasyāḥ sā rājīvalocanā
samasa.explanation: The two members stand in a comparison: rājīva 'lotus' is the standard of comparison (upamāna) and locana 'eye' what is compared. The whole describes Her as a bahuvrīhi, 'She whose eyes are (like) lotuses'; locana takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: usually the blue or the red lotus
locana, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose eyes are like lotuses
names.significance: The lotus-eye is the classical image of beauty and tenderness; traditionally Her glance is said to bless as a lotus opens to the sun.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'rAjiva' put into IAST and the sentence tidied.

components.note: √rañj 'to color, redden; to please' with the agent suffix -ana (lyu) and feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who delights the mind
names.significance: The root rañj means both 'to color' and 'to delight'. Traditionally it is said that Her crimson radiance tints even the white Śiva, and that She colors the mind with joy.
names.uncertain: The root allows two senses, 'one who colors (reddens)' and 'one who delights'; the meaning gives the second, the significance the first.

components.meaning: delightful woman; she who gives joy
components.note: √ram 'to delight, sport' with the agent suffix -ana (lyu) and feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who gives joy
names.significance: Ramaṇī is also an ordinary word for a beautiful woman; traditionally She is the one who delights in Her play of creation and makes Her devotees rejoice.

components.meaning: to be relished; full of flavor and delight
components.note: from rasa 'taste, essence, delight' (or √ras) with the suffix -ya, feminine

names.meaning: She who is to be relished, the essence of all delight
names.significance: The Taittirīya Upaniṣad says of the Real, raso vai saḥ, 'It is rasa itself; having gained rasa one becomes blissful'. She is that essence, the delight that is tasted in every delight.

meaning_check.note: rasyā 'to be relished' is passive in sense; 'She who enjoys' does not follow from the form and is dropped.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over a karmadhāraya with a dropped middle member and an inner karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: रणन्त्यः किङ्किण्यः रणत्किङ्किण्यः; रणत्किङ्किणीभिः युक्ता मेखला रणत्किङ्किणिमेखला; रणत्किङ्किणिमेखला यस्याः सा रणत्किङ्किणिमेखला
samasa.vigraha_iast: raṇantyaḥ kiṅkiṇyaḥ raṇatkiṅkiṇyaḥ; raṇatkiṅkiṇībhiḥ yuktā mekhalā raṇatkiṅkiṇimekhalā; raṇatkiṅkiṇimekhalā yasyāḥ sā raṇatkiṅkiṇimekhalā
samasa.explanation: (1) raṇat-kiṅkiṇi 'tinkling bells': the present participle raṇat qualifies kiṅkiṇi (karmadhāraya). (2) …kiṅkiṇi-mekhalā 'a girdle set with tinkling bells': a karmadhāraya whose middle word 'yukta, furnished with' is understood (madhyamapadalopin). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi describing Her: 'She whose girdle has tinkling bells'.

components.note: kiṅkiṇī, also kiṅkiṇi; worn on girdles and anklets

names.meaning: She who wears a girdle of tinkling bells
names.significance: Traditionally the soft sound of the bells announces Her presence; the girdle belongs to the description of Her form.

components.meaning: delight; the delightful one; a name of Lakṣmī

names.meaning: She who is Ramā (Lakṣmī)
names.significance: Ramā, 'she who delights', is a standard name of Lakṣmī, goddess of fortune; here Lalitā is Lakṣmī Herself.

meaning_check.note: Sarasvatī is not in the name: ramā is a name of Lakṣmī. ITRANS 'lakShmI' removed.

names.uncertain: The earlier rendering added Sarasvatī; that rests on a commentarial derivation I could not confirm, so it is left out.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: ā + i → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi of comparison (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: राकायाः इन्दुः राकेन्दुः; राकेन्दुः इव वदनम् यस्याः सा राकेन्दुवदना
samasa.vigraha_iast: rākāyāḥ induḥ rākenduḥ; rākenduḥ iva vadanam yasyāḥ sā rākenduvadanā
samasa.explanation: (1) rākā-indu 'the moon of the full-moon night', i.e. the full moon (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi of comparison: 'She whose face (vadana) is like the full moon'; vadana takes the feminine -ā.

components.meaning: the night of the full moon

components.note: vadana, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose face is like the full moon
names.significance: The full moon is whole, cool and radiant without glare: so is Her face. Traditionally, the moon lacking nothing points to Her as the fullness that never wanes.

meaning_check.note: 'delightful' is not in the name; rākā-indu is the full moon.

names.previous_split_issues: rākendu was left as one row; it is rākā 'full-moon night' + indu 'moon', joined by guṇa (ā + i → e).

samasa.vigraha: रतिः रूपम् यस्याः सा रतिरूपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: ratiḥ rūpam yasyāḥ sā ratirūpā
samasa.explanation: rati 'Rati, delight' and rūpa 'form' are co-referential, and the compound describes Her: 'She whose form is Rati'. It may equally be taken as a karmadhāraya in apposition ('She who is Rati in form'); the sense is the same.

components.meaning: Rati, wife of Kāma; love, delight

names.meaning: She who is in the form of Rati, the wife of Kāma
names.significance: Rati is the delight of love personified, the consort of Kāma; traditionally every delight is a form of Hers.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'kAma' put into IAST; Rati capitalized as a name.

names.previous_split_issues: rati was glossed only 'love/pleasure'; here it is first the goddess Rati, Kāma's wife.

samasa.vigraha: रतिः प्रिया यस्याः सा रतिप्रिया; अथवा रतेः प्रिया रतिप्रिया
samasa.vigraha_iast: ratiḥ priyā yasyāḥ sā ratipriyā; athavā rateḥ priyā ratipriyā
samasa.explanation: As a bahuvrīhi, Rati (or delight) is dear to Her: 'She to whom Rati is dear', i.e. who is fond of Rati. As a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, priyā 'beloved' is the head and Rati stands in the genitive: 'She who is dear to Rati'. The members are simply juxtaposed.

names.meaning: She who is fond of Rati
names.significance: Traditionally Rati, being dear to Her, attends on Her; read inwardly, She delights in the joy of Her devotees.

meaning_check.note: 'served by Rati' is not in the grammar; the second reading of the compound ('dear to Rati') is given in the samāsa note.

names.uncertain: Bahuvrīhi ('to whom Rati is dear') and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa ('dear to Rati') are both possible; rati may also be the common noun 'delight'.

samasa.vigraha: रक्षाम् करोति इति रक्षाकरी
samasa.vigraha_iast: rakṣām karoti iti rakṣākarī
samasa.explanation: The second member karī is an agent form of √kṛ 'to make' that exists only with a preceding object word (upapada): 'she who makes protection'. The suffix ṭa (Pāṇini 3.2.20) makes the feminine end in -ī.

components.note: √kṛ 'to do' with the agent suffix ṭa, feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who is the protector
names.significance: She protects the worlds She has made; traditionally, the protection is above all from fear and from bondage.

samasa.vigraha: राक्षसान् हन्ति इति राक्षसघ्नी
samasa.vigraha_iast: rākṣasān hanti iti rākṣasaghnī
samasa.explanation: ghnī is an agent form of √han 'to strike, slay', used only after its object (upapada): 'she who slays the rākṣasas'. With the suffix (ṭak) the root is reduced to ghn- and the feminine ends in -ī.

components.note: √han 'to slay', reduced to ghn- before the suffix; feminine

names.meaning: She who slays the demons
names.significance: Traditionally, outwardly the demons of the Purāṇic wars, inwardly the dark tendencies (lust, anger, greed) that oppose the devotee.

meaning_check.note: 'the entire race of' is not in the name; the plural object is implied, but the wording is simplified.

names.meaning: She who gives delight
names.significance: Rāmā is also a common word for a woman; traditionally every woman is seen as Her form, as the Devī Māhātmya says in its hymn to Nārāyaṇī (striyaḥ samastāḥ sakalā jagatsu).

samasa.vigraha: रमणे लम्पटा रमणलम्पटा
samasa.vigraha_iast: ramaṇe lampaṭā ramaṇalampaṭā
samasa.explanation: lampaṭā 'eagerly devoted, passionately attached' is the head; the object of the attachment, ramaṇa 'the beloved', stands to it in the locative ('devoted to'). The members are simply juxtaposed.

names.meaning: She who is passionately devoted to Her beloved, Lord Śiva
names.significance: Traditionally the beloved is Kāmeśvara; Her devotion to Him is the model of the devotee's own longing.

meaning_check.note: 'Lord of Her heart' is not in the name; ramaṇa 'beloved' is rendered directly, and ITRANS 'shiva' put into IAST.

names.uncertain: ramaṇa can be the beloved (Śiva) or the act of love-play itself ('eager for love-play'); the meaning follows the first.

components.note: √kam 'to desire' (or kāma) with the gerundive suffix -ya, feminine

names.meaning: She who is to be desired
names.significance: Traditionally She is the one goal worth desiring, sought above all by those who seek liberation; every other desire is a distant reflection of the longing for Her.

samasa.vigraha: कामस्य कला कामकला; कामकला रूपम् यस्याः सा कामकलारूपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: kāmasya kalā kāmakalā; kāmakalā rūpam yasyāḥ sā kāmakalārūpā
samasa.explanation: (1) kāma-kalā 'the kalā (subtle digit, power) of Kāma' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose form is the kāmakalā'. kāmakalā can also be analysed as a dvandva, Kāma and Kalā, i.e. Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī together.

components.meaning: Kāma, desire; in Śrīvidyā Kāmeśvara, the supreme Śiva

names.meaning: She who is in the form of Kāmakalā
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā the kāmakalā is the most subtle form of the Goddess: the triangle of three bindus (sun, moon and fire) with the half-digit below, the union of Śiva and Śakti from which the Śrīcakra and the mantra unfold. Puṇyānanda's Kāmakalāvilāsa is devoted to it.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'kAmakalA' put into IAST.

names.previous_split_issues: kalā was glossed 'art/digit' without the technical sense; kāmakalā is a single doctrinal term.
names.uncertain: kāmakalā is analysed both as 'the digit of Kāma' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa) and as 'Kāma and Kalā' (dvandva).

samasa.vigraha: कदम्बस्य कुसुमानि कदम्बकुसुमानि; कदम्बकुसुमानि प्रियाणि यस्याः सा कदम्बकुसुमप्रिया
samasa.vigraha_iast: kadambasya kusumāni kadambakusumāni; kadambakusumāni priyāṇi yasyāḥ sā kadambakusumapriyā
samasa.explanation: (1) kadamba-kusuma 'the flowers of the kadamba tree' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi with priya 'dear' as its predicate: 'She to whom kadamba flowers are dear'; priya takes the feminine -ā.

components.meaning: the kadamba tree (Neolamarckia cadamba), with round, fragrant orange blossoms

names.meaning: She who is fond of kadamba flowers
names.significance: Her abode in Maṇidvīpa lies within a kadamba forest (name 60, kadambavanavāsinī), and kadamba blossoms adorn Her ears (name 21).

meaning_check.note: 'especially' is not in the name.

names.previous_split_issues: kadamba was glossed 'kadamba flower'; it is the tree, and kusuma supplies 'flower'.

names.meaning: She who is auspicious
names.significance: She is auspiciousness itself, and so the giver of all that is good; traditionally kalyāṇī also means 'beautiful'.

meaning_check.note: kalyāṇī means 'auspicious'; 'bestows' is causative and not in the word (it is given as the consequence under significance).

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (the final member made feminine to agree with Her)
samasa.vigraha: जगत्याः कन्दः जगतीकन्दः; सा जगतीकन्दा
samasa.vigraha_iast: jagatyāḥ kandaḥ jagatīkandaḥ; sā jagatīkandā
samasa.explanation: kanda 'bulbous root' is the head and jagatī 'the world' stands to it in the genitive: 'the root of the world'. Because the name is in apposition to the Goddess, kanda takes the feminine -ā.

names.meaning: She who is the root of the whole world
names.significance: As a plant springs from its bulb and is sustained by it, the world sprouts from Her and is nourished by Her.

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya), the final member made feminine
samasa.vigraha: करुणा एव रसः करुणारसः; करुणारसस्य सागरः करुणारससागरः; सा करुणारससागरा
samasa.vigraha_iast: karuṇā eva rasaḥ karuṇārasaḥ; karuṇārasasya sāgaraḥ karuṇārasasāgaraḥ; sā karuṇārasasāgarā
samasa.explanation: (1) karuṇā-rasa 'the rasa that is compassion' (karmadhāraya of identification): compassion is both a liquid essence and the aesthetic sentiment (rasa) of pathos. (2) …rasa-sāgara 'the ocean of that essence' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) In apposition to Her, sāgara takes the feminine -ā.

names.meaning: She who is an ocean of the nectar of compassion
names.significance: The ocean is limitless and never exhausted however much is drawn from it; so is Her compassion.

meaning_check.note: rasa, the essence or nectar of compassion, was not translated.

names.meaning: She who possesses all the arts
names.significance: The kalās are the sixty-four arts (compare name 236, catuḥṣaṣṭikalāmayī) and also the sixteen digits of the moon; She possesses them all, and they are Hers to bestow.

meaning_check.note: -vatī means 'possessing'; 'embodiment' is closer to -mayī. The tradition's sense is kept.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: कलः आलापः यस्याः सा कलालापा
samasa.vigraha_iast: kalaḥ ālāpaḥ yasyāḥ sā kalālāpā
samasa.explanation: kala 'soft, sweet, melodious' qualifies ālāpa 'speech, discourse', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose speech is sweet and soft'. ālāpa takes the feminine -ā.

names.meaning: She who speaks musically and sweetly
names.significance: Name 27 says the sweetness of Her speech puts to shame the vīṇā (kacchapī) of Sarasvatī; traditionally Her speech is gentle even when it commands.
names.uncertain: The fused ā allows kalā 'art' + ālāpa as well: 'She whose talk is of the arts'. The usual reading takes kala 'sweet'.

names.meaning: She who is beautiful
names.significance: Kāntā is literally 'the desired one': She is beautiful and the beloved of Kāmeśvara; traditionally Her beauty is the radiance (kānti) of consciousness.

samasa.vigraha: कादम्बरी प्रिया यस्याः सा कादम्बरीप्रिया
samasa.vigraha_iast: kādambarī priyā yasyāḥ sā kādambarīpriyā
samasa.explanation: kādambarī is the subject and priyā 'dear' its predicate within the compound, and the whole describes Her: 'She to whom kādambarī is dear'.

components.meaning: kādambarī, a liquor distilled from kadamba blossoms; mead

names.meaning: She who is fond of kādambarī, the kadamba-flower wine
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā ritual, offerings of wine have an inner sense: the nectar of bliss that flows when kuṇḍalinī reaches the crown.

meaning_check.note: 'mead' replaced by the name of the drink itself, kādambarī, with its kadamba origin.

samasa.vigraha: वरम् ददाति इति वरदा
samasa.vigraha_iast: varam dadāti iti varadā
samasa.explanation: dā is an agent form of √dā 'to give' used only after its object (Pāṇini 3.2.3 āto 'nupasarge kaḥ: suffix ka after roots in ā): 'she who gives boons'. It takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: √dā 'to give' with the suffix ka, feminine

names.meaning: She who grants boons
names.significance: The boon-granting gesture (varada-mudrā) is one of the classical hand-poses of the Goddess; traditionally She grants even more than is asked.

meaning_check.note: 'generously' is not in the name.

samasa.vigraha: वामे नयने यस्याः सा वामनयना
samasa.vigraha_iast: vāme nayane yasyāḥ sā vāmanayanā
samasa.explanation: vāma 'beautiful' qualifies nayana 'eye', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose eyes are beautiful'; nayana takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: nayana, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who has beautiful eyes
names.significance: vāma also means 'left': traditionally a hint that She is the left half of Śiva.
names.uncertain: vāma means both 'beautiful' and 'left'; the meaning takes the first.

samasa.vigraha: वारुण्याः मदः वारुणीमदः; वारुणीमदेन विह्वला वारुणीमदविह्वला
samasa.vigraha_iast: vāruṇyāḥ madaḥ vāruṇīmadaḥ; vāruṇīmadena vihvalā vāruṇīmadavihvalā
samasa.explanation: (1) vāruṇī-mada 'the intoxication of vāruṇī' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The adjective vihvalā 'overcome, reeling' is the head, and the intoxication stands to it in the instrumental as the cause.

components.meaning: vāruṇī, a wine (said to have risen from the churned ocean, hence Varuṇa's)

names.meaning: She who is overcome by the intoxication of vāruṇī
names.significance: Traditionally read inwardly: the rapture of the bliss of the Self, which leaves one heedless of the world.

meaning_check.note: The name says 'overcome by the intoxication of vāruṇī'; 'ambrosial drink' and ITRANS 'vAruNi' replaced.

names.previous_split_issues: vāruṇī mada was one row and the last member was misspelled vivhalā; it is vāruṇī + mada + vihvalā (ह्व).

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: विश्वस्मात् अधिका विश्वाधिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: viśvasmāt adhikā viśvādhikā
samasa.explanation: adhikā 'exceeding, greater' is the head and viśva 'the universe' stands to it in the ablative of comparison: 'greater than the universe'.

names.meaning: She who transcends the universe
names.significance: As the Puruṣasūkta says of the Person, all beings are one quarter of Him and three quarters are immortal beyond; She pervades the universe and exceeds it.

samasa.vigraha: वेदैः वेद्या वेदवेद्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: vedaiḥ vedyā vedavedyā
samasa.explanation: vedyā 'to be known' (gerundive of √vid) is the head, and veda stands to it in the instrumental as the means: 'to be known through the Vedas'.

components.note: √vid 'to know' with the gerundive suffix -ya, feminine

names.meaning: She who is to be known through the Vedas
names.significance: As Kṛṣṇa says in the Bhagavad Gītā (15.15), 'I alone am to be known by all the Vedas' (vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyaḥ); the whole of the Veda points to Her.

meaning_check.note: vedyā is a gerundive, 'to be known'; Vedas capitalized.

names.previous_split_issues: veda was glossed 'Vedas/knowledge' and vedyā 'knowable'; the instrumental relation ('through the Vedas') was not shown.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: विन्ध्यः एव अचलः विन्ध्याचलः; विन्ध्याचले निवसति इति विन्ध्याचलनिवासिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: vindhyaḥ eva acalaḥ vindhyācalaḥ; vindhyācale nivasati iti vindhyācalanivāsinī
samasa.explanation: (1) vindhya-acala 'the Vindhya mountain' (karmadhāraya of apposition: the mountain that is Vindhya). (2) nivāsin 'dwelling' is an agent noun from ni + √vas with the suffix ṇini (Pāṇini 3.2.78 supy ajātau ṇinis tācchīlye), compounded with its place in the locative sense: 'she who dwells on the Vindhya mountain'; feminine -inī.

components.meaning: the Vindhya range of central India

names.meaning: She who resides in the Vindhya mountains
names.significance: In the Devī Māhātmya (ch. 11) the Goddess foretells that She will be born of Yaśodā and dwell on the Vindhya mountain (vindhyācalanivāsinī); She is worshipped there as Vindhyavāsinī.

meaning_check.note: Vindhya capitalized.

names.previous_split_issues: vindhyācala was left as one row; it is vindhya + acala 'mountain', with the a + a fused.

components.note: vi + √dhā 'to place, establish' + the agent suffix -tṛ, feminine -trī

names.meaning: She who creates and sustains this universe
names.significance: vidhātṛ is a name of Brahmā as creator and ordainer; dhātrī also means a nurse or mother. She both ordains the world and nourishes it.

meaning_check.note: Typo 'unverse' corrected.

samasa.vigraha: वेदानाम् जननी वेदजननी
samasa.vigraha_iast: vedānām jananī vedajananī
samasa.explanation: jananī 'mother, she who gives birth' is the head and the Vedas stand to it in the genitive: 'the mother of the Vedas'.

components.note: √jan 'to be born', causative, with -ana and feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who is the mother of the Vedas
names.significance: The Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad says the Ṛg, Yajur and Sāma Vedas are the breath of the Great Being; traditionally the Vedas issue from Her as Her breath.

meaning_check.note: Vedas capitalized.

samasa.vigraha: विष्णोः माया विष्णुमाया
samasa.vigraha_iast: viṣṇoḥ māyā viṣṇumāyā
samasa.explanation: māyā is the head and Viṣṇu stands to it in the genitive: 'the māyā of Viṣṇu'. The members are simply juxtaposed.

components.meaning: māyā, the power that veils and projects; illusion

names.meaning: She who is the illusory power (māyā) of Viṣṇu
names.significance: The Devī Māhātmya (ch. 5) hails the Goddess 'who in all beings is called Viṣṇumāyā' (yā devī sarvabhūteṣu viṣṇumāyeti śabditā): the power by which even the all-pervading Lord appears in forms.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'viShNu' put into IAST and māyā named.

names.meaning: She who is playful
names.significance: Traditionally the universe is Her play (vilāsa, līlā); the play is the projecting power by which the One appears as the many.

samasa.vigraha: क्षेत्रम् स्वरूपम् यस्याः सा क्षेत्रस्वरूपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: kṣetram svarūpam yasyāḥ sā kṣetrasvarūpā
samasa.explanation: kṣetra 'the field' and svarūpa 'own form, nature' are co-referential, and the whole describes Her: 'She whose own form is the field'. svarūpa itself is sva 'own' + rūpa 'form'.

components.meaning: field; in the Gītā's sense, the body and all of matter

names.meaning: She whose very form is the field (kṣetra), the body and all matter
names.significance: The Bhagavad Gītā (ch. 13) calls the body, and all of prakṛti, the field (kṣetra), and the one who knows it the knower of the field (kṣetrajña). Names 341–345 develop that teaching.

meaning_check.note: 'body is matter' blurred the term: kṣetra is the Gītā's 'field', which the gloss now names.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; alternatively the feminine of a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa by association (puṃyoga)
samasa.vigraha: क्षेत्रस्य ईशी क्षेत्रेशी; अथवा क्षेत्रस्य ईशः क्षेत्रेशः तस्य पत्नी क्षेत्रेशी
samasa.vigraha_iast: kṣetrasya īśī kṣetreśī; athavā kṣetrasya īśaḥ kṣetreśaḥ tasya patnī kṣetreśī
samasa.explanation: Read directly, īśī 'ruler' is the head and kṣetra stands to it in the genitive: 'the sovereign of the field'. Read the other way, kṣetreśa 'Lord of the field' is Śiva, and kṣetreśī is his consort, the feminine formed by association with the husband (Pāṇini 4.1.48 puṃyogād ākhyāyām).

names.meaning: She who is the Sovereign of the field (kṣetra)
names.significance: She rules over every body and the whole field of matter, as the inner controller; traditionally She is also the consort of Śiva, the Lord of the field.

meaning_check.note: The previous 'wife of Kṣetreśa (Śiva)' is the second analysis of the compound, given in the samāsa note; the meaning takes the direct reading. ITRANS removed.

names.uncertain: The name may mean 'ruler of the field' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa) or 'wife of Kṣetreśa, Śiva' (puṃyoga feminine); both are current.

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner itaretara-dvandva and an upapada-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: क्षेत्रम् जानाति इति क्षेत्रज्ञः; क्षेत्रम् च क्षेत्रज्ञः च क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञौ; क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोः पालिनी क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञपालिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: kṣetram jānāti iti kṣetrajñaḥ; kṣetram ca kṣetrajñaḥ ca kṣetrakṣetrajñau; kṣetrakṣetrajñayoḥ pālinī kṣetrakṣetrajñapālinī
samasa.explanation: (1) kṣetra-jña 'the knower of the field' (upapada-tatpuruṣa; jña from √jñā with the suffix ka, Pāṇini 3.2.3). (2) kṣetra-kṣetrajña 'the field and the knower of the field' (itaretara-dvandva). (3) pālinī 'protector' is the head and the pair stands to it in the genitive.

components.meaning: the knower of the field: the conscious self

names.meaning: She who protects both the field and the knower of the field
names.significance: The field is the body and the world; its knower is the conscious self. She guards both: matter and spirit, body and soul.

meaning_check.note: The long previous gloss ('protector of matter and the knower of matter, therefore … body and soul') is condensed; the Gītā's terms are kept and the interpretation moved to significance.

sandhi.rule: the s of the prefix nis becomes r (through ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ) before a voiced sound

samasa.vigraha: क्षयः च वृद्धिः च क्षयवृद्धी; क्षयवृद्धिभ्याम् विनिर्मुक्ता क्षयवृद्धिविनिर्मुक्ता
samasa.vigraha_iast: kṣayaḥ ca vṛddhiḥ ca kṣayavṛddhī; kṣayavṛddhibhyām vinirmuktā kṣayavṛddhivinirmuktā
samasa.explanation: (1) kṣaya-vṛddhi 'decay and growth' (itaretara-dvandva). (2) The participle vinirmuktā 'wholly freed' is the head and the pair stands to it in the ablative: 'freed from decay and growth'.

components.note: vi + nis + √muc 'to release', past participle, feminine

names.meaning: She who is free from growth and decay
names.significance: The moon waxes and wanes; traditionally She is the sixteenth digit of the moon, which neither grows nor wanes, and the Self that is untouched by birth and death.

samasa.vigraha: क्षेत्रम् पालयति इति क्षेत्रपालः; क्षेत्रपालेन समर्चिता क्षेत्रपालसमर्चिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: kṣetram pālayati iti kṣetrapālaḥ; kṣetrapālena samarcitā kṣetrapālasamarcitā
samasa.explanation: (1) kṣetra-pāla 'guardian of the field' (upapada-tatpuruṣa; pāla from √pāl 'to protect' with the suffix aṇ). (2) The participle samarcitā 'well worshipped' is the head and Kṣetrapāla stands to it in the instrumental as the agent.

names.meaning: She who is worshipped by Kṣetrapāla, guardian of the sacred field
names.significance: Kṣetrapāla is the guardian deity of a temple precinct, a form of Bhairava (Śiva). Traditionally a Purāṇic story is told here: after Kālī slew the demon Dāruka, Śiva took the form of an infant to draw off Her fury, and that child is Kṣetrapāla.

meaning_check.note: 'Śiva in infant form' is the Purāṇic story, not the name; it moves to significance. ITRANS removed.

names.previous_split_issues: kṣetra-pāla was split into two rows glossed 'field/body' and 'guardian' with no sign that together they name a deity.
names.uncertain: The story of the infant Kṣetrapāla is traditionally told on this name; I could not confirm its Purāṇic source, so it is not attributed.

names.meaning: She who is ever-victorious
names.significance: The prefix vi- intensifies: Her victory is complete and unique. Vijayā is also a name of Durgā and one of the Nityā goddesses of the lunar fortnight.

samasa.vigraha: विगतम् मलम् यस्याः सा विमला
samasa.vigraha_iast: vigatam malam yasyāḥ sā vimalā
samasa.explanation: The prefix vi- stands for vigata 'gone away', and the compound describes Her: 'She from whom impurity has gone'; mala takes the feminine -ā.

names.meaning: She who is without a trace of impurity
names.significance: In Śaiva and Śākta thought the soul is bound by three impurities (āṇava, māyīya and kārma mala); She is untouched by any of them, and frees those who worship Her.

components.meaning: to be saluted, worthy of reverence
components.note: √vand 'to salute, praise' with the gerundive suffix -ya, feminine

names.meaning: She who is adorable, worthy of worship
names.significance: She is to be saluted by all, the gods included; traditionally the salutation itself is a form of Her worship.

samasa.vigraha: वन्दारवः जनाः वन्दारुजनाः; वन्दारुजनेषु वत्सला वन्दारुजनवत्सला
samasa.vigraha_iast: vandāravaḥ janāḥ vandārujanāḥ; vandārujaneṣu vatsalā vandārujanavatsalā
samasa.explanation: (1) vandāru-jana 'people given to worship' (karmadhāraya). (2) vatsalā 'tenderly loving' is the head and the worshippers stand to it in the locative: 'loving towards those who bow to Her'.

components.meaning: tenderly loving (as a cow to her calf)

names.meaning: She who is full of motherly love for those who worship Her
names.significance: vatsala is the love of a cow for her calf: She runs to the devotee who bows to Her as a mother to her child.

meaning_check.note: Typo 'motherlly' corrected.

sandhi.rule: the final c of vāc becomes a velar at the end of a member (Pāṇini 8.2.30 coḥ kuḥ), voiced to g before v by jaśtva (8.2.39): vāg-

samasa.vigraha: वाचम् वदति इति वाग्वादिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: vācam vadati iti vāgvādinī
samasa.explanation: vādinī is an agent noun from √vad 'to speak' with the suffix ṇini, compounded with its object vāc 'speech': 'she who utters speech'. Feminine -inī.

components.meaning: speech, word; the goddess of speech

names.meaning: She who gives voice to all speech
names.significance: The Kena Upaniṣad speaks of 'that which is not uttered by speech, by which speech is uttered' (yad vācānabhyuditaṃ yena vāg abhyudyate). Vāgvādinī is also the name invoked in the mantra of Sarasvatī (vada vada vāgvādini).

meaning_check.note: 'She who speaks' was too thin for vāc + vādinī, 'utterer of speech'.

names.previous_split_issues: vāg was given in its sandhi form; the stem is vāc (g only by sandhi).

samasa.vigraha: वामाः केशाः यस्याः सा वामकेशी
samasa.vigraha_iast: vāmāḥ keśāḥ yasyāḥ sā vāmakeśī
samasa.explanation: vāma 'beautiful' qualifies keśa 'hair', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose hair is beautiful'. Because keśa is a part of the body, the feminine may end in -ī (Pāṇini 4.1.54 svāṅgāc copasarjanād asaṃyogopadhāt).

components.note: keśa, with the feminine -ī of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who has beautiful hair
names.significance: Traditionally also read as the consort of Vāmakeśa (Śiva); the Vāmakeśvara Tantra is one of the root texts of Śrīvidyā (compare name 945, vāmakeśvarī).
names.uncertain: Read as a bahuvrīhi ('beautiful-haired') or as the consort of Vāmakeśa, Śiva; the meaning takes the first.

samasa.vigraha: वह्नेः मण्डलम् वह्निमण्डलम्; वह्निमण्डले वसति इति वह्निमण्डलवासिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: vahneḥ maṇḍalam vahnimaṇḍalam; vahnimaṇḍale vasati iti vahnimaṇḍalavāsinī
samasa.explanation: (1) vahni-maṇḍala 'the disc (region) of fire' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) vāsinī 'dwelling', an agent noun from √vas with the suffix ṇini, is compounded with its place in the locative sense: 'she who dwells in the region of fire'.

names.meaning: She who resides in the disc of fire
names.significance: Traditionally the body holds three regions, of fire, sun and moon; the region of fire is placed at the base of the spine, where kuṇḍalinī sleeps.

samasa.vigraha: कल्पा लतिका कल्पलतिका; भक्तिमताम् कल्पलतिका भक्तिमत्कल्पलतिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: kalpā latikā kalpalatikā; bhaktimatām kalpalatikā bhaktimatkalpalatikā
samasa.explanation: (1) kalpa-latikā 'the wish-fulfilling creeper': kalpa, as in kalpa-vṛkṣa 'the tree that grants whatever is wished', qualifies latikā (karmadhāraya). (2) The creeper is the head and bhaktimat 'those who have devotion' stands to it in the genitive: 'the wish-granting creeper of the devotees'. The t of bhaktimat stands unchanged before k.

names.meaning: She who is the wish-granting creeper for Her devotees
names.significance: The kalpa creeper of Indra's heaven yields whatever is wished; She gives Her devotees all they seek, and in the end Herself.

meaning_check.note: 'kalpa (wish-granting) creeper' tidied into English.

samasa.vigraha: पशूनाम् पाशाः पशुपाशाः; पशुपाशान् विमोचयति इति पशुपाशविमोचिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: paśūnām pāśāḥ paśupāśāḥ; paśupāśān vimocayati iti paśupāśavimocinī
samasa.explanation: (1) paśu-pāśa 'the bonds of the bound souls' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) vimocinī 'releaser', an agent noun from the causative of vi + √muc with the suffix ṇini, is compounded with its object: 'she who loosens those bonds'.

components.meaning: a bound soul (lit. a tethered animal)

names.meaning: She who frees bound souls (paśu) from their bonds (pāśa)
names.significance: In Śaiva and Śākta thought the soul bound by impurity is a paśu, its fetters are pāśa, and the Lord is Paśupati; She cuts those fetters.

meaning_check.note: 'the ignorant' and 'bondage' sharpened to the technical paśu 'bound soul' and pāśa 'bond'.

sandhi.rule: m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ); before h it remains anusvāra
savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya and a nañ-bahuvrīhi)
samasa.vigraha: न शेषः येषाम् ते अशेषाः; अशेषाः पाषण्डाः अशेषपाषण्डाः; संहृताः अशेषपाषण्डाः यया सा संहृताशेषपाषण्डा
samasa.vigraha_iast: na śeṣaḥ yeṣām te aśeṣāḥ; aśeṣāḥ pāṣaṇḍāḥ aśeṣapāṣaṇḍāḥ; saṃhṛtāḥ aśeṣapāṣaṇḍāḥ yayā sā saṃhṛtāśeṣapāṣaṇḍā
samasa.explanation: (1) a-śeṣa 'with nothing left over, all' (nañ-bahuvrīhi). (2) aśeṣa-pāṣaṇḍa 'all the heretics' (karmadhāraya). (3) The participle saṃhṛta 'destroyed' is placed first, as is usual for a participle in a bahuvrīhi, and the whole describes Her: 'She by whom all heretics have been destroyed'.

components.note: sam + √hṛ 'to take', past participle; appears as saṃhṛta- in the compound
pāṣaṇḍa, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She by whom all heretics have been destroyed
names.significance: Traditionally pāṣaṇḍas are those who abandon dharma and mislead others; inwardly, She destroys hypocrisy and false views in the devotee.

meaning_check.note: saṃhṛta is a past participle in a bahuvrīhi: 'by whom … have been destroyed'.

names.previous_split_issues: saṃhṛtāśeṣa was one row glossed 'completely destroyed'; it is saṃhṛta 'destroyed' + aśeṣa 'all', and aśeṣa belongs with pāṣaṇḍa.

sandhi.rule: jaśtva: a final t becomes d before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte)

samasa.vigraha: सन् आचारः सदाचारः; सदाचारस्य प्रवर्तिका सदाचारप्रवर्तिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: san ācāraḥ sadācāraḥ; sadācārasya pravartikā sadācārapravartikā
samasa.explanation: (1) sat-ācāra 'good conduct' (karmadhāraya; sat 'good, true'). (2) pravartikā 'one who sets in motion' is the head and good conduct stands to it in the genitive (as the object of the agent noun).

components.note: pra + √vṛt, causative, + the agent suffix -aka; a → i before -kā (Pāṇini 7.3.44)

names.meaning: She who establishes and promotes right conduct
names.significance: Traditionally She upholds the dharma taught in the Veda and the conduct of the good, and inspires others to follow it.

meaning_check.note: 'immersed in' is not in the name; pravartikā means 'one who sets in motion'.

names.previous_split_issues: sadācāra was one row; it is sat 'good' + ācāra 'conduct' (t voiced to d).

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), which takes the place of articulation of the following stop (8.4.58–59 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ): written n before a dental

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-, tṛtīyā- and karmadhāraya compounds)
samasa.vigraha: तापानाम् त्रयम् तापत्रयम्; तापत्रयम् एव अग्निः तापत्रयाग्निः; तापत्रयाग्निना सन्तप्ताः तापत्रयाग्निसन्तप्ताः; तापत्रयाग्निसन्तप्तानाम् समाह्लादनी चन्द्रिका तापत्रयाग्निसन्तप्तसमाह्लादनचन्द्रिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: tāpānām trayam tāpatrayam; tāpatrayam eva agniḥ tāpatrayāgniḥ; tāpatrayāgninā santaptāḥ tāpatrayāgnisantaptāḥ; tāpatrayāgnisantaptānām samāhlādanī candrikā tāpatrayāgnisantaptasamāhlādanacandrikā
samasa.explanation: (1) tāpa-traya 'the triad of afflictions' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) …traya-agni 'the fire that is that triad' (karmadhāraya of identification). (3) …agni-santapta 'scorched by that fire' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa): those who suffer. (4) samāhlādana 'gladdening' (agent noun in -ana) takes them as its object (genitive relation) and qualifies candrikā 'moonlight' (karmadhāraya): 'the moonlight that gladdens those scorched …'. In composition the feminine agent noun stands in its stem form.

names.meaning: She who is the moonlight that gives joy to those burned by the triple fire of misery
names.significance: The three afflictions are those arising from oneself (ādhyātmika), from other beings (ādhibhautika) and from the powers of nature (ādhidaivika). As moonlight cools after the heat of day, She brings relief.
names.previous_split_issues: trayāgni was one row glossed 'three fires'; the triad belongs with tāpa (tāpa-traya 'the three afflictions'), and that triad is then called a fire.

names.meaning: She who is ever young
names.significance: She is beyond time and so never ages; traditionally She is pictured always in the bloom of youth, with the freshness of a girl of sixteen (ṣoḍaśī).

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: तापसैः आराध्या तापसाराध्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: tāpasaiḥ ārādhyā tāpasārādhyā
samasa.explanation: ārādhyā 'to be worshipped' (gerundive) is the head and the ascetics stand to it in the instrumental as the agents.

names.meaning: She who is worshipped by ascetics
names.significance: Those who practise austerity seek Her; traditionally, tapas undertaken without Her is said to bear no fruit.

samasa.vigraha: तनु मध्यम् यस्याः सा तनुमध्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: tanu madhyam yasyāḥ sā tanumadhyā
samasa.explanation: tanu 'slender' qualifies madhya 'middle, waist', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose waist is slender'; madhya takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: madhya, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is slender-waisted
names.significance: The slender waist belongs to the classical picture of beauty; traditionally it also suggests the subtle, scarcely visible link between the manifest and the unmanifest.

sandhi.rule: s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66), ru becomes u after a and before a (6.1.113 ato ror aplutād aplute), a + u → o by guṇa (6.1.87), and the following a merges into the o (6.1.109 eṅaḥ padāntād ati), marked by the avagraha ऽ

samasa.vigraha: तमः अपहन्ति इति तमोऽपहा
samasa.vigraha_iast: tamaḥ apahanti iti tamo'pahā
samasa.explanation: apahā is an agent form of apa + √han 'to strike away' (suffix ḍa, with the root reduced to -ha) used after its object: 'she who strikes away darkness'. Feminine -ā.

components.meaning: darkness; tamas, the quality of inertia and ignorance

components.note: apa + √han 'to strike' with the suffix ḍa, feminine

names.meaning: She who dispels darkness, the ignorance of tamas
names.significance: The prayer 'lead me from darkness to light' (tamaso mā jyotir gamaya, Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad) is answered by Her.

meaning_check.note: 'born of tamas' is not in the name: tamas is itself the darkness that She removes.

components.note: √cit 'to perceive, be conscious' + the suffix -ti (ktin), nominative

names.meaning: She who is Consciousness itself
names.significance: The first sūtra of Kṣemarāja's Pratyabhijñāhṛdaya reads citiḥ svatantrā viśvasiddhihetuḥ, 'Consciousness, free, is the cause of the accomplishment of the universe'. With this name begins a run of names on Her as pure consciousness.

meaning_check.note: 'pure intelligence' replaced by 'consciousness', the sense of citi.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over inner karmadhārayas), the final member made feminine
samasa.vigraha: तत् इति पदम् तत्पदम्; लक्ष्यः अर्थः लक्ष्यार्थः; तत्पदस्य लक्ष्यार्थः तत्पदलक्ष्यार्थः; सा तत्पदलक्ष्यार्था
samasa.vigraha_iast: tat iti padam tatpadam; lakṣyaḥ arthaḥ lakṣyārthaḥ; tatpadasya lakṣyārthaḥ tatpadalakṣyārthaḥ; sā tatpadalakṣyārthā
samasa.explanation: (1) tat-pada 'the word tat' (karmadhāraya of apposition: the word that is 'tat'). (2) lakṣya-artha 'the indicated (implied) meaning' (karmadhāraya). (3) The implied meaning is the head and the word stands to it in the genitive. In apposition to Her the final member takes the feminine -ā.

components.meaning: that; the word 'tat' of tat tvam asi

names.meaning: She who is the implied meaning (lakṣyārtha) of the word 'tat' (That)
names.significance: In the great saying tat tvam asi ('You are That', Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.8.7), Vedānta takes 'tat' not in its literal sense (the omniscient Lord with attributes) but in its implied sense, pure consciousness free of qualities; She is that implied meaning. Names 425–427 return to the same saying.

meaning_check.note: 'the embodiment of truth' missed the technical term: lakṣyārtha is the meaning reached by implication (lakṣaṇā), as opposed to the literal meaning (vācyārtha).

names.previous_split_issues: tatpada and lakṣyārthā were glossed loosely; lakṣyārtha is the Vedāntic 'implied meaning' (lakṣya + artha, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha).

sandhi.rule: jaśtva: a final t becomes d before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte)

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (over an inner karmadhāraya) with the possessive suffix -in
samasa.vigraha: एकः रसः एकरसः; चित् एव एकरसः चिदेकरसः; चिदेकरसः रूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति चिदेकरसरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: ekaḥ rasaḥ ekarasaḥ; cit eva ekarasaḥ cidekarasaḥ; cidekarasaḥ rūpam asyāḥ asti iti cidekarasarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) eka-rasa 'a single, uniform essence' (karmadhāraya). (2) cit-ekarasa 'the uniform essence that is consciousness' (karmadhāraya of identification). (3) It is compounded with rūpa 'form', and the possessive suffix -in makes rūpiṇī 'having as form': 'She whose form is consciousness alone, one undivided essence'.

names.meaning: She whose nature is consciousness alone, one undivided essence
names.significance: Ekarasa is 'of one taste throughout': as the Bṛhadāraṇyaka's lump of salt is salty through and through, She is consciousness through and through, with nothing else mixed in.

meaning_check.note: 'She who is the cause of knowledge' is not in the name, and ekarasa 'one undivided essence' was not translated.

names.previous_split_issues: cid was given in its sandhi form (the stem is cit), and ekarasa was glossed 'sole essence' as one row; it is eka 'one' + rasa 'essence'.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over a gati-compound with cvi, ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas and an inner bahuvrīhi)
samasa.vigraha: स्वस्य आत्मा स्वात्मा; स्वात्मनः आनन्दः स्वात्मानन्दः; अलवः लवः भूता लवीभूता; स्वात्मानन्दस्य लवीभूता स्वात्मानन्दलवीभूता; ब्रह्मा आदिः येषाम् ते ब्रह्मादयः; ब्रह्मादीनाम् आनन्दः ब्रह्माद्यानन्दः; ब्रह्माद्यानन्दानाम् सन्ततिः ब्रह्माद्यानन्दसन्ततिः; स्वात्मानन्दलवीभूता ब्रह्माद्यानन्दसन्ततिः यस्याः सा स्वात्मानन्दलवीभूतब्रह्माद्यानन्दसन्ततिः
samasa.vigraha_iast: svasya ātmā svātmā; svātmanaḥ ānandaḥ svātmānandaḥ; alavaḥ lavaḥ bhūtā lavībhūtā; svātmānandasya lavībhūtā svātmānandalavībhūtā; brahmā ādiḥ yeṣām te brahmādayaḥ; brahmādīnām ānandaḥ brahmādyānandaḥ; brahmādyānandānām santatiḥ brahmādyānandasantatiḥ; svātmānandalavībhūtā brahmādyānandasantatiḥ yasyāḥ sā svātmānandalavībhūtabrahmādyānandasantatiḥ
samasa.explanation: (1) sva-ātman 'Her own Self' and svātma-ānanda 'the bliss of Her own Self' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas; ātman loses its n in composition). (2) lavībhūta 'become a mere particle': lava 'particle' takes the suffix cvi, which turns its a into ī (Pāṇini 7.4.32 asya cvau) and expresses 'becoming what it was not', and it is compounded with bhūta as a gati (1.4.61 ūryādicviḍācaś ca); the bliss of Her Self stands to it in the genitive ('a particle of …'). (3) brahma-ādi 'Brahmā and the others' (bahuvrīhi), brahmādi-ānanda 'their bliss', and …ānanda-santati 'the whole succession of those blisses' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi describing Her: 'She for whom the whole range of the bliss of Brahmā and the other gods has become a mere particle of the bliss of Her own Self'. santati is feminine, so the name ends in -iḥ.

names.meaning: She for whom the whole range of bliss of Brahmā and the other gods is but a particle of the bliss of Her own Self
names.significance: The Taittirīya Upaniṣad measures bliss in steps, each a hundredfold the one before, up to the bliss of Brahmā, and all of it is a fraction of the bliss of Brahman; the Bṛhadāraṇyaka says other beings live on a particle of that bliss. Her own bliss is that whole.

meaning_check.note: The previous gloss turned the bahuvrīhi into an action ('makes … insignificant'); the name says that the bliss of the gods has become a particle of Hers. ITRANS 'brahmA' removed.

names.previous_split_issues: svātmānanda, lavībhūta and brahmādyānanda were each left fused; lavībhūta is lava 'particle' + cvi + bhūta 'become', and brahmādya- is brahma + ādi, with i → y before ānanda.

verse_notes.note: Names 305–320 (to the end of śloka 72) all begin with ra/rā; the next ślokas group names by initial sound in the same way: k in 73–74 (except 325 jagatīkandā), v in 74–75 and 77, kṣ in 76, t in 79. Name 305 divides rāja-rāja + arcitā ('worshipped by the king of kings').
Name 313 ramā is a name of Lakṣmī; 319 rāmā (long first ā) is a different word, 'delightful woman'.
Name 322 kāmakalā is a technical term of Śrīvidyā, the subtle triangular form of the Goddess, not 'the art of love'.
Name 333 is one compound, vāruṇī-mada-vihvalā (spelled ह्व, vihvalā); the printed source had split it and misspelled it.
Names 341–345 all begin with kṣ and take up the Bhagavad Gītā's teaching of the field (kṣetra) and the knower of the field (kṣetrajña).
Name 350 vāgvādinī: the stem is vāc 'speech'; its c appears as g before v.
Name 355 divides saṃhṛta + aśeṣa + pāṣaṇḍā; the long ā joins saṃhṛta and aśeṣa.
Name 357 fills the whole first half. In 361 tamo'pahā the avagraha (ऽ) marks the a of apahā absorbed into the o of tamo.

external_sandhi.rule: visarga becomes s before t (Pāṇini 8.3.34 visarjanīyasya saḥ)

verse_notes.note: citiḥ (362) is a name on its own; the s of citis- is its visarga before tat-. Names 362–365 open a run of Vedāntic names; 365 fills the whole second half.

report.summary: Checked all 61 names of ślokas 71–80 against text.json: sandhi at every member and visible prefix junction, layered samāsa analyses with pausa-form vigraha-vākyas, and the meanings against that analysis. Most changes are tidying (ITRANS, capitalization, typos) or removing words not in the name; two meanings were replaced (363 tatpadalakṣyārthā, which names the Vedāntic 'implied meaning' of tat, and 364 cidekarasarūpiṇī, whose 'cause of knowledge' is not in the name). Old splits often left fused members as one row (rājārcitā, trayāgni, saṃhṛtāśeṣa, lavībhūta) or gave stems in their sandhi form (vāg, cid). No problem was found in the Sanskrit text; the only external sandhi is citiḥ + tat- in śloka 80.
